items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: Janis Joplin. Because Albert Grossman had his studio here and he ran the record company that they all recorded for and, you know, he was sort of the reigning champion at the time. And everybody also played here in a little place called the Espresso Café.

ctx.x: But most of the musicians on that festival lived here. You know, like Jimi [Hendrix] lived here and Dylan lived here and The Band lived here. They all lived here. Janis Joplin. Because Albert Grossman had his studio here and he ran the record company that they all recorded for and, you know, he was sort of the reigning champion at the time. And everybody also played here in a little place called the Espresso Café. Yeah. So in a way it did have more to do with Woodstock than people might think.
Okay. When you were getting into jazz in Germany and then in France, you sort of entered the jazz world at the bebop stage. Is that correct?
